questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines article.

questions.proof: The capital, and its main port, is Kingstown.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines article.

questions.proof: The country speaks English as its official language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Grenadines islands lie between the islands of Saint Vincent in the north and _____ in the south.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “north”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: It lies to the west of Barbados, south of Saint Lucia and north of Grenada in the Windward Islands of the Lesser Antilles.

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “capital”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines article, under the heading “Administrative divisions”.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1763 by the Treaty of _____, France gave control of Saint Vincent to Britain; France took the island again in 1779, but the British then regained Saint Vincent under the Treaty of Versailles (1783).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “France”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In 1763 by the Treaty of Paris, France gave control of Saint Vincent to Britain; France took the island again in 1779, but the British then regained Saint Vincent under the Treaty of Versailles (1783).
